section: Industrial sickness - meaning, causes, consequences and remedial measures
subsections: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: The Tiwari Committee, which investigated industrial sickness and recommended special legislation, was associated with which period?
accepted.x: The Tiwari Committee investigated industrial sickness during 1984-85 and recommended special legislation, leading to the enactment of SICA, 1985.
accepted.tq: Use the date attached to the committee before linking it to the legislation.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Tiwari Committee's recommendations led to the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the legislation year from the later year in which BIFR began functioning.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was set up in:
accepted.x: BIFR was created under SICA and was set up in January 1987, functioning from 1987.
accepted.tq: Separate the enactment year of SICA from the establishment year of BIFR.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: Appeals against the decisions of the BIFR lay before the:
o: Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
accepted.x: The Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction, or AAIFR, heard appeals against BIFR decisions.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the old appellate authority and the later NCLAT.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the functions associated with BIFR?
o: Early detection of sickness, revival of viable units and closure of unviable units
Regulation of stock exchanges, revival of banks and promotion of exports
Recovery of all agricultural loans and supervision of public-sector recruitment
Promotion of small-scale industries, control of inflation and management of foreign exchange
accepted.x: BIFR was concerned with early detection of industrial sickness, revival of viable units and closure or winding-up of unviable units.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that combines the three functions rather than a neighbouring economic responsibility.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the coverage of SICA, 1985:
1. It covered companies with industrial undertakings.
2. It applied only to public-sector companies.
3. It covered private companies also.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SICA covered companies with industrial undertakings in both the public and private sectors. Therefore, statements 1 and 3 are correct, while statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Watch for the extreme word 'only' in the statement about public-sector coverage.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a reason for the failure of the BIFR-based regime?
o: Legal loopholes enabling promoters to stall debt recovery
Excessively rapid resolution of all sick units
accepted.x: The regime was criticised for procedural delays, legal loopholes and an ineffective revival mechanism; rapid resolution was not a reason for its failure.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented criticism of the institution.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: BIFR ceased to exist on:
accepted.x: BIFR ceased on 30 November 2016. BIFR and AAIFR were dissolved from 1 December 2016.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the cessation date from the following date of dissolution and transition.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: With effect from 1 December 2016, pending cases before BIFR and AAIFR were referred to which institutions under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
accepted.x: After BIFR and AAIFR were dissolved, pending cases were referred to the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal under IBC, 2016.
accepted.tq: Match the old institutions with their correct successor forums, not with regulatory or banking bodies.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. SICA, 1985
 b. BIFR
 c. AAIFR
 d. Debtor-in-possession

List-II
 i. Creditor-in-control under the new regime
 ii. National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
 iii. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
 iv. National Company Law Tribunal

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: SICA corresponds to the earlier regime replaced by IBC, BIFR was succeeded by NCLT, AAIFR by NCLAT, and debtor-in-possession was replaced by creditor-in-control.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure institutional successor pairs and eliminate codes with a repeated mismatch.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the present insolvency framework?
o: IBBI — appellate tribunal for BIFR cases
accepted.x: NCLT functions as the adjudicating authority under the present framework. IBBI is the regulator and insolvency professionals are licensed under the framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct authority-function pair while rejecting swapped institutional roles.
accepted.sec: BIFR and AAIFR - set-up, functions, abolition, successor forum

accepted.s: Under the original SICA, 1985 definition, an industrial company could be treated as sick only when it had been registered for at least:
accepted.x: The original SICA definition required the industrial company to have been registered for at least seven years.
accepted.tq: Do not substitute the amended five-year threshold for the original SICA threshold.
accepted.sec: Definition of sick unit - SICA 1985 and RBI definition for MSMEs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the original SICA, 1985 definition of a sick industrial company:
1. Accumulated losses had to equal or exceed net worth at the end of a financial year.
2. Cash losses in that financial year and the preceding financial year were relevant.
3. The company had to have been registered for at least seven years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The original definition included all three conditions: at least seven years of registration, accumulated losses equal to or exceeding net worth, and cash losses in the relevant and preceding years.
accepted.tq: Combine the threshold, loss and cash-loss conditions before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Definition of sick unit - SICA 1985 and RBI definition for MSMEs

accepted.s: Which change was introduced by the 1993 amendment to the SICA definition of a sick company?
o: The registration requirement was increased to ten years and cash losses were retained.
The registration requirement was reduced to three years and net worth was excluded.
The registration requirement was abolished and accumulated losses were ignored.
The registration requirement was reduced to five years and the cash-loss test was dropped.
accepted.x: The 1993 amendment reduced the minimum registration period from seven to five years and dropped the cash-loss test.
accepted.tq: Compare the original and amended definitions by isolating both changed elements.
accepted.sec: Definition of sick unit - SICA 1985 and RBI definition for MSMEs

accepted.s: In the general economic sense, a unit is considered sick when it:
o: Records a temporary fall in sales but remains financially self-sustaining
Fails to generate a surplus on a continuing basis and depends on repeated infusion of funds
Has a high level of exports and foreign exchange earnings
Receives a government subsidy for modernisation
accepted.x: Industrial sickness generally refers to the inability to generate surplus continuously and dependence on repeated infusion of funds.
accepted.tq: Choose the definition based on continuing financial dependence rather than a temporary business fluctuation.
accepted.sec: Definition of sick unit - SICA 1985 and RBI definition for MSMEs

accepted.s: Under the RBI definition for micro and small units, which of the following could indicate sickness?
o: Any borrowal account remaining NPA for more than three months
A 10 per cent rise in net worth through retained earnings
A single month of delayed sales without an NPA
A temporary increase in working capital
accepted.x: Under the stated RBI definition, a borrowal account remaining NPA for more than three months was one indicator of sickness.
accepted.tq: Focus on the precise NPA duration rather than a general reference to financial difficulty.
accepted.sec: Definition of sick unit - SICA 1985 and RBI definition for MSMEs

accepted.s: A micro or small unit could also be treated as sick under the RBI definition when its net worth had eroded by at least:
accepted.x: The RBI definition included erosion of net worth by 50 per cent through accumulated losses in the previous year.
accepted.tq: Use the exact percentage threshold and distinguish it from nearby percentage distractors.
accepted.sec: Definition of sick unit - SICA 1985 and RBI definition for MSMEs

accepted.s: The RBI's Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation of MSMEs, introduced in 2016, emphasised:
o: Early identification of incipient stress and Committees for Stressed MSMEs
Replacement of all bank loans by government grants
Automatic closure of every account classified as NPA
accepted.x: The 2016 framework replaced the earlier definition with early identification of incipient stress through SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2 categories and Committees for Stressed MSMEs.
accepted.tq: Select the option expressing the preventive and early-warning approach of the framework.
accepted.sec: Definition of sick unit - SICA 1985 and RBI definition for MSMEs

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the National Renewal Fund?
o: To provide export subsidies exclusively to private companies
To regulate the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India
To compensate and retrain workers displaced during industrial restructuring and support modernisation
To finance only the acquisition of agricultural land
accepted.x: The fund provided VRS compensation, retraining and redeployment for displaced workers and supported industrial restructuring and modernisation.
accepted.tq: Apply the fund's social-safety-net purpose to a restructuring situation.
accepted.sec: National Renewal Fund - purpose, beneficiaries

accepted.s: The principal beneficiaries of the National Renewal Fund were:
o: Employees of the Reserve Bank of India
Workers of sick or restructured units, mainly in public-sector enterprises
Only foreign investors in special economic zones
accepted.x: The fund primarily benefited workers of sick or restructured units, especially workers in public-sector enterprises.
accepted.tq: Separate the beneficiaries from the wider industrial objectives of the fund.
accepted.sec: National Renewal Fund - purpose, beneficiaries

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an INTERNAL cause of industrial sickness?
accepted.x: Diversion of funds is an internal management-related cause. Demand contraction, power shortages and regulatory changes are external causes.
accepted.tq: Classify the cause by asking whether it originates within the firm's management.
accepted.sec: Causes - internal vs external

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I: Causes of industrial sickness
 a. Poor working-capital management
 b. Aggressive competition
 c. Obsolete technology
 d. Sudden changes in export-import policy

List-II: Classification
 i. Internal production cause
 ii. External demand cause
 iii. Internal finance cause
 iv. External policy cause

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Poor working-capital management is an internal finance cause; aggressive competition is an external demand cause; obsolete technology is an internal production cause; and export-import policy changes are external policy causes.
accepted.tq: Start by pairing the clear internal finance and external policy examples, then complete the classification.
accepted.sec: Causes - internal vs external

accepted.s: For MSMEs, delayed payments by which of the following are identified as a major trigger of industrial sickness?
accepted.x: Delayed payments by large buyers and government departments create serious cash-flow problems and are a major trigger of sickness among MSMEs.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific creditor relationship rather than treating all delayed payments as equivalent.
accepted.sec: Causes - internal vs external

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of industrial sickness:
1. Bank loans may turn into non-performing assets.
2. Plant, land and funds may remain idle in unviable units.
3. Industrial sickness can cause unemployment.
4. It necessarily increases revenue receipts of the exchequer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Sickness can create NPAs, unemployment and locked capital. Idle assets also result in revenue loss to the exchequer, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed fiscal consequence and retain the three direct consequences.
accepted.sec: Consequences - NPAs, unemployment, locked capital

accepted.s: The State takeover of certain sick private units, particularly in textiles and engineering, was primarily intended to:
o: Transfer all industrial land to banks
accepted.x: The State took over certain sick private units, especially textile and engineering units, mainly to protect jobs and employment.
accepted.tq: Link the policy intervention to its stated employment objective rather than ownership alone.
accepted.sec: Consequences - NPAs, unemployment, locked capital

accepted.s: Which institution, set up in 1971, was associated with the rehabilitation of sick industrial units?
o: Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
accepted.x: The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India, established in 1971, was set up to rehabilitate sick industrial units.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its rehabilitation role and distinguish it from later forums.
accepted.sec: Rehabilitation measures - RBI revival framework, restructuring schemes

accepted.s: The Liberalized Margin Money Scheme, introduced in June 1987, was associated with:
o: Regulating delayed payments by government departments
Reducing sickness in the small-scale sector
Providing compensation only to retrenched public-sector workers
accepted.x: The Liberalized Margin Money Scheme, introduced in June 1987, helped reduce sickness in the small-scale sector.
accepted.tq: Use the scheme's date and sectoral objective together to avoid confusing it with later MSME measures.
accepted.sec: Rehabilitation measures - RBI revival framework, restructuring schemes

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the one-time restructuring measure for stressed MSME loans?
o: It was introduced in 2016 and prohibited all forms of restructuring.
It was introduced in 2019 without downgrade and extended during 2020-21.
It was introduced in 1987 and applied only to large public-sector companies.
It was introduced in 1992 and permanently cancelled all MSME loans.
accepted.x: A one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans without downgrade was permitted in 2019 and extended during 2020-21.
accepted.tq: Track the measure through both its introduction year and extension period.
accepted.sec: Rehabilitation measures - RBI revival framework, restructuring schemes

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the present institutional arrangement for dealing with industrial distress and delayed MSME payments?
o: National Renewal Fund for companies, and IRBI for delayed payments
SICA through BIFR for companies, and AAIFR for delayed payments
NCLAT for all delayed payments, and RBI for winding-up companies
IBC 2016 through NCLT for companies, and MSME Samadhaan for delayed payments
accepted.x: The present framework uses IBC, 2016 and NCLT for company insolvency matters, while MSME Samadhaan addresses delayed payments to MSMEs.
accepted.tq: Separate the insolvency forum from the mechanism dealing specifically with delayed MSME payments.
accepted.sec: Rehabilitation measures - RBI revival framework, restructuring schemes

accepted.s: Industrial sickness has been particularly concentrated in which group of sectors?
accepted.x: The sectors especially associated with industrial sickness are textiles, including cotton mills, jute, sugar and engineering.
accepted.tq: Recall the sectoral cluster rather than selecting a group of generally important industries.
accepted.sec: Sick industries by sector

accepted.s: The absorption of sick private textile and engineering units by the public sector had which consequence?
o: It increased the net worth of every public-sector enterprise.
It eliminated all unemployment in the industrial sector.
It lowered the returns of public-sector enterprises.
It ended the need for industrial restructuring.
accepted.x: The public sector absorbed sick private textile and engineering units to protect jobs, but this lowered the returns of public-sector enterprises.
accepted.tq: Trace the stated trade-off between employment protection and public-sector returns.
accepted.sec: Sick industries by sector
